text:
Jack Quinn is playing like a first-line forward in a contract year, and the role backs it up. He's at 19:04 a night, up from 15:39 last season, and on the ice for 81% of Buffalo's power-play time (37% last year). That's a breakout by our definition: 19 points in 19 games, a point a game against 0.62 last season. The Athletic has already asked what his next deal costs the Sabres.

Some of the scoring will cool. He's shooting 17.3%, and our talent range has him closer to 13% over time. The underlying chances are up too, though (1.11 expected goals per 60 from 0.96), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 54% of his shots coming off the rush last season. He is a transition player getting more transition minutes.

The caution flag is defensive. Evolving-Hockey had opponents generating more with him on the ice last season than with almost any other forward. Five on five this year, Buffalo is roughly even with him out there, which is progress worth tracking.
headline: Jack Quinn picked the right year
